task.title: Overflow protection
task.prompt: Inputs are already required to be finite numbers; make results finite too. If any calculation produces a result that is not a finite number, raise ValueError with a helpful message and keep the console running. Preserve all existing operations, input validation, and quit behavior.
task.description: Stop the calculator from reporting infinite results.

data.summary: Added a check in calculate() to raise ValueError if the result is not finite, preventing infinite or NaN results from being reported.

data.summary: The proposed change adds a check in the calculate function to ensure that the result of any operation is finite, raising a ValueError if not. This prevents the calculator from reporting infinite or NaN results, as required. The implementation is correct and preserves all existing operations, input validation, and quit behavior. Edge cases such as overflow (e.g., very large numbers) and invalid operations (e.g., inf - inf) are now handled gracefully.
limitations: The check only applies to the result of a single operation; chained calculations or future extensions may require similar checks.
The error message is generic and does not specify the exact cause (overflow vs. invalid operation).
The function still allows extremely large but finite results, which may not be practical in all contexts.
